newsitem.title: UK: U.S rates top concern for emerging mkt debt - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S rates top concern for emerging mkt debt - survey.

text.p: Emerging market fixed income investors are more concerned about U.S. Treasury market volatility than country risk, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

It said almost 80 percent of those surveyed expect a 25 percent basis point rate increase by the U.S. Federal Reserve in May, with 54 percent expecting 75 basis points or more of Fed tightening for the entire year.

The survey, taken between March 16 and April 21, covered investors managing $14.3 billion of emerging markets debt. Some 26 percent of respondents were dedicated fund managers, and 28 percent hedge fund managers.
"Political risk is seen as a cause of greater concern than economic factors, but less than global liquidity concerns," Merrill said.

Respondents ranked their level of concern between one and 10 about various risks. Higher U.S. rates and Treasury market volatility rated highest with 74 percent ranking the level of risk at seven or above.
Only 27 percent saw social unrest and reform fatigue at a risk level of over five, and devaluation risks were ranked at five.
The level of risk associated with elections and political transitions was ranked at 5.5.
Other areas of concern were European and Japanese interest rates, the formation of EMU, and the possibility of capital flight from Russia.

The survey found investors expected to realise total annualised returns averaging 12.6 percent this year for Brady bonds and eurobonds, compared to 15.4 percent when the survey was last taken in October 1996.
Despite expecting lower returns, investors were not panicked about the outlook for Bradys or U.S. Treasuries. It said the year-end forecast for Treasuries was 7.11 percent.
Those with allocations to local currency instruments expect to receive slightly higher returns averaging 14.7 percent for a diversified portfolio of emerging markets local currency debt.

Merrill said the fastest growing segment in emerging markets debt was sovereign local currency instruments, which it estimated now comprised 63 percent of the total $1.159 trillion emerging market debt universe.

"Given the heightened concern about further Fed tightening, local currency holdings are a promising diversification tool given the near-zero correlation with U.S. Treasuries compared to the 43 percent correlation of Brady bonds."
The survey said the best performance in the year was expected to be concentrated in Latin America, with Argentina, Mexico and Venezuela seen having the most favourable prospects.
Respondents also said that Russian debt could have the greatest degree of spread tightening of over 100 basis points despite mixed views about current trends in the country.
The survey found some respondents bearish on Venezuela, which was ranked behind Brazil and with Ecuador as having the worst prospects.

Investors appeared to have raised their exposure to corporate debt, with 75 percent owning both sovereign and corporate debt against 65 percent in October. Some 25 percent of those portfolios include corporate debt.
